## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-blind: the reviewer does not know the author's identity and the author does not know the reviewer's. | Stage | Allowed? | Notes |

## Format

> Sources: the journal's PDF "How to prepare your submission" (version January 2026, read directly), the aims page (Wayback copy 2026-05-02) and the submission guidelines page (Wayback copy 2026-10-03); URLs under Identity and Policies. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Original articles, empirical or conceptual; critical reviews, accepted only through the annual special-issue call; meta-analyses; critical essays (aims copy 2026-05-02). The guidelines copy 2026-10-03 says review papers sent through the regular route are desk rejected automatically. The journal does not publish book reviews (live policies page, 2026-11-23; same in the 2025-05-03 copy). A 2023 editorial on crafting review and essay articles is cited by the journal for detailed guidance: https://doi.org/10.1177/00187267221148440 (not read) |
| **Word limit** | 13,000 words in total including abstract, text, endnotes, references and appendices, excluding tables and figures (PDF, January 2026). The aims copy words it as including abstract, keywords and references. An older publisher-hosted guidelines copy (2025-07-15, https://web.archive.org/web/20250715161353/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/HUM) asks for a Word file of at most 45 correctly formatted pages |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The PDF says manuscripts exceeding the limit or formatted incorrectly are sent back for reformatting; no exception procedure found |
| **Abstract limit** | 100 to 200 words; keywords: 3 or 4 main key phrases plus at least 3 or 4 further keywords (PDF, section 9) |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap; references count inside the 13,000 words. Sage Harvard style (PDF, section 18) |
| **Supplementary material** | Online-only supplementary material allowed; reviewers need not read it and it must not be used just to stay within the word limit; it must be submitted to the journal directly, with no external links in the manuscript (PDF, section 7) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. One figure or table per page; tables and figures single-spaced, everything else double-spaced; 300 dpi minimum for raster images (PDF, sections 5 and 15) |
| **Anonymisation and other submission rules** | Manuscript, and any response to the decision letter, must be anonymised (see Peer Review). Page format: Times New Roman 12 point, 2.54 cm margins, double-spaced, each component on a new page. A rejected paper may not be resubmitted unless the action editor invites it; an author may submit no more than two single-authored manuscripts to the journal in any 12-month period, with at least six months between submissions of single-authored manuscripts (guidelines copy 2026-10-03 and live policies page 2026-11-23). A cover letter describes which works in the journal the paper connects to (PDF section 3). Papers using a dataset already used elsewhere must submit the related papers and a data transparency matrix (live policies page 2026-11-23; same in the 2025-05-03 copy) |

### Orientation

> Counts come from Crossref records of this journal published 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23: 388 journal-article records (editorials and other non-article items included), of which 340 (87.6%) carry an abstract. A hit is a record with an abstract whose title or abstract matches the regular expression (case-insensitive, word boundaries; every expression is in the keyword register in the AI-Research Notes); shares use 340 as the denominator. Counts are lower bounds because 48 records have no abstract. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Empirical designs dominate by keyword: "qualitative-any" (qualitative, case study, ethnograph*, interview) 121 of 340 (35.6%) and "quant-designs-any" (quantitative, survey, regression and panel terms, multilevel, structural equation, mediation or moderation, time-lagged or multi-wave, diary, meta-analysis) 95 (27.9%) against "theory-building-any" (conceptual, theorizing, essay, theory building) 45 (13.2%); these overlap. The aims copy (2026-05-02) says the journal accepts both empirical and conceptual articles and "both quantitative and qualitative approaches" |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Both are well represented: "interview" 54 (15.9%), "qualitative" 41 (12.1%), "ethnograph*" 32 (9.4%), "survey" 25 (7.4%), "time-lagged/multi-wave" 37 (10.9%), "multilevel/multi-level" 18 (5.3%) |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | The aims copy says the journal welcomes manuscripts that cross disciplinary boundaries and encourages research relating social theory to practice that aims to improve working lives. The journal's "in and around work" scope is stated in the same text. Sage files it under "Management and Organization Studies" on its discipline list (publisher home copy 2025-07-16) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes, stated by the journal: articles must advance knowledge with a strong theoretical and/or empirical contribution to the literature on work relationships and organizational work processes, and "papers that do not directly address these processes are unlikely to be suitable". Source: aims page, Wayback copy 2026-05-02, https://web.archive.org/web/20260502100140/https://www.humanrelationsjournal.org/about/aims-scope/. Retrieved 2026-11-23.
- **What kind of engagement?** Original articles must be grounded in, and positioned within or against, the relevant literature (aims copy). The guidelines ask authors to connect to works previously published in the journal and to say in the cover letter which works they take forward (guidelines copy 2026-10-03, PDF section 3, https://www.humanrelationsjournal.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Human-Relations-How-to-prepare-your-submission-Jan-2026-1.pdf). Conceptual papers must show how they advance or challenge existing scholarly conversations.
- **Content the guidelines say is unsuitable:** articles that merely offer scores or describe relationships between chosen measures, unless they critique a tool of analysis; student simulation exercises as the sole basis of a paper; papers mainly about research design or instruments; "poor standard of English" is less likely to be reviewed (guidelines copy 2026-10-03).
- **Data expectations stated by the journal:** new empirical data are not required, but for empirical papers suitable data are necessary and not sufficient; single-respondent cross-section designs are named as the most common reason for rejecting quantitative papers; the journal wants to move away from papers with only a limited number of interviews without contextual or comparative information, while allowing small interview numbers in exploratory, tightly focused or detail-intensive designs (guidelines page, copy 2026-10-03).
- **Special issues:** an annual call for special issue proposals and a dedicated annual special issue for critical reviews are listed (journal home copy 2026-10-19; aims copy 2026-05-02).
- **Consequences of ignoring it:** the journal states that its editorial team desk rejects about half of all articles received, and that review papers sent through the regular route are desk rejected automatically (guidelines copy 2026-10-03). The statistics page states 3% accepted of 1,587 submissions in 2025 (live, 2026-11-23) and 3% of 1,415 submissions in 2023 (copy 2026-04-14).

### Methodological Preferences

> Scores follow this pass's own convention, not an external standard: share of the 340 abstract records (2021-2026, Crossref) whose title or abstract matches the expression; 0 hits = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement. The journal's own text says it welcomes both qualitative and quantitative methods and "encourages" strong methods, particularly longitudinal designs (guidelines copy 2026-10-03), and states no ranking of methods, so no row exceeds 3. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how reviewers judge it. The schema's rows were kept where they fit; where they do not fit a management venue, this is said. Expressions are in the register in the AI-Research Notes.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Qualitative case study | 2 | "case study" 12 of 340 (3.5%); "qualitative" 41 (12.1%); "qualitative-any" 121 (35.6%) |
| Ethnography / fieldwork | 3 | "ethnograph*" 32 (9.4%) (does not match "autoethnography") |
| Qualitative interviews | 3 | "interview" 54 (15.9%). The journal states it wants interview studies with enough evidential weight and contextual or comparative information (guidelines copy 2026-10-03) |
| Survey / quantitative analysis | 3 | "quant-designs-any" 95 (27.9%); "survey" 25 (7.4%); "quantitative" 2 (0.6%); "regression/panel/econometric" 5 (1.5%); "multilevel/multi-level" 18 (5.3%); "structural equation/mediation/moderation" 41 (12.1%); the journal names single-respondent cross-section designs as the most common reason for rejecting quantitative papers (guidelines copy 2026-10-03) |
| Multi-wave / longitudinal designs (added row) | 3 | "time-lagged/multi-wave" 37 (10.9%); "longitudinal" 15 (4.4%, score 2 alone). The guidelines say they encourage longitudinal design |
| Quantitative experimental | 2 | "experimental" 15 (4.4%); the pattern does not separate laboratory from field experiments. The guidelines say student-only simulations cannot be the sole basis of a paper |
| Autoethnography | 1 | "autoethnograph*" 2 (0.6%) |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | "theory-building-any" 45 (13.2%): "conceptual" 15 (4.4%), "theorizing" 26 (7.6%), "essay" 5 (1.5%). The aims copy states conceptual papers must make a substantive theoretical contribution |
| Mixed methods | 1 | "mixed methods" 3 (0.9%) |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 1 | "meta-analysis" 3 (0.9%) in abstracts; "review-any" (systematic review, literature review, meta-analysis, bibliometric, scoping review) 8 (2.4%). The journal lists meta-analyses and critical reviews as accepted types, with critical reviews only through the annual special-issue call (aims copy 2026-05-02), so the count understates stated openness |
| Archival / historical analysis (added row) | 2 | "archival/historical" 10 (2.9%) |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. Observation from the 340 abstracts (Crossref, 2021-2026), matching the abstract text alone (not the title; recomputed 2026-11-23): 316 (92.9%) contain a first-person word (I, my, we, our), nearly all plural; 21 (6.2%) contain singular I or my. Among 32 single-author records with an abstract, 19 use singular I or my and 21 use any first-person form. For comparison, title plus abstract gives 318 (93.5%) any first person, 31 (9.1%) singular, and 20 and 22 among the 32 single-author records; the extra singular hits include titles, so the figures above are abstract-only. Newest examples: https://doi.org/10.1177/00187267261500257 and https://doi.org/10.1177/00187267261499126 (any first person), https://doi.org/10.1177/00187267261504293 (singular). The anonymisation rule asks authors to cite their own earlier work in the third person (PDF, section 2). Plural "we" may be a convention of collective authorship rather than a stance |
| **Expected density** | Length ceiling 13,000 words including abstract and references, excluding tables and figures (PDF section 6). The guidelines ask for a short methods section: "not too long", with detail moved to an appendix or supplement (guidelines copy 2026-10-03). No article-length statistics were gathered |
| **Abstract and keywords** | Abstract of 100-200 words covering topic, questions, participants, methods, results, analysis, conclusions, practical implications and future research; the journal asks for abstracts readable by non-specialists and encourages posing a question or clear claim; 3 or 4 key phrases plus at least 3 or 4 additional keywords (PDF section 9) |
| **Writing style notes** | British or US spelling if consistent; three heading levels; numbers below ten written out; quotations kept to a minimum and to 100 words or fewer where possible; notes at the end before references, not footnotes; author-date citations and Sage Harvard references; avoid italics and quote marks for terms; "clear English comprehensible to readers outside of their area of specialism" (PDF sections 10-18; guidelines copy 2026-10-03). Section order of articles was not sampled |
| **Authorship pattern** | Crossref author counts over 388 records (347 list authors; 41 list none): 1 author 36, 2 authors 88, 3 authors 111, 4 or more 112 (retrieved 2026-11-23). Singly authored records are 10.4% of the 347 |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | Blank. The journal pages and PDF read contain no ethics-approval or consent rule; they ask only that the manuscript state whether pseudonyms were used for people and organizations and require release forms for images of identifiable people or workplaces (PDF section 4; Sage guidelines copy 2025-07-15). The publisher's general ethics policy was not read |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author submissions are limited: at most two single-authored manuscripts per author in any 12-month period, at least six months apart (guidelines copy 2026-10-03, https://web.archive.org/web/20261003175028/https://www.humanrelationsjournal.org/journal/submission-guidelines/). The live policies and guidelines pages (2026-11-23) add that the Co-Editors-in-Chief may decline manuscripts where a pattern of unusually frequent submissions involves overlapping author teams, even if the team composition varies (https://www.humanrelationsjournal.org/journal/our-policies/). Single-author records are 36 of 347 Crossref records that list authors (10.4%) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Blank. No rule or count found; the pages read say nothing on unaffiliated authors |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Journal-specific: if a dataset has produced other papers, the submission must include those manuscripts and a data transparency matrix listing the variables, or for qualitative work the quotations and observations, used in each and their overlap, updated when papers under review elsewhere progress; violation is grounds for rejection (live policies page, 2026-11-23, https://www.humanrelationsjournal.org/journal/our-policies/; same text in the 2025-05-03 copy). The PDF (https://www.humanrelationsjournal.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Human-Relations-How-to-prepare-your-submission-Jan-2026-1.pdf) repeats a table of commonality for shared datasets (section 3) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-blind with strict anonymisation: no author names, no acknowledgements, third-person citation of own work, no external links to supplementary material, and no "Author, year" placeholders (PDF section 2 and 7). Prior online publication is barred except institutional repository and conference proceedings (PDF section 3), and a preprint server is not named either way (https://www.humanrelationsjournal.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Human-Relations-How-to-prepare-your-submission-Jan-2026-1.pdf) |
| **AI use** | Live policies page (2026-11-23): AI use only for copy editing or proofing, declared at submission and in the cover letter (not in the manuscript), statement requested if accepted, unacknowledged use is grounds for rejection or retraction (https://www.humanrelationsjournal.org/journal/our-policies/). The 2025-05-03 copy had a different rule (cover letter and methods section, no AI-generated datasets) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; APC not read (OpenAlex lists USD 3900 / GBP 2859, unverified); 195 of 385 works from 2021-2026 are hybrid open access in OpenAlex |
| **Other** | The journal does not publish book reviews; translations of articles only through Sage-supported services at the requester's cost (live policies page, 2026-11-23; same in the 2025-05-03 copy) |

### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**signal_quality (0-5)**: overall 3. Per layer: Crossref keyword counts (methods, topics, voice) 4 (388 records, 87.6% with abstracts, counts are lower bounds); OpenAlex metrics and country counts 4; publisher-wide policies 3 (Wayback copies dated 2024); journal-specific policies and guidelines 4 for the PDF (read directly, version January 2026) and 3 for the Wayback copies of the journal site (2025-05 to 2026-10); experiential layer 1 (SciRev n=2, self-selected, no calendar dates).

**Per-subsection state (for the promotion gate)**: all seven subsections rest on counts or archived journal text. Reviewer behaviour, review time beyond n=2, reviewer-recommendation rules, ethics approval rules, independent-scholar rules and the APC stay blank. The journal-reported 3% acceptance (2025 live; 2023 in the older copy) and "about half desk rejected" statements are the strongest experiential facts and are single statements from the journal.

**Method.** Crossref records: `https://api.crossref.org/journals/0018-7267/works` (also via `works?filter=issn:0018-7267,from-pub-date:2021-01-01,until-pub-date:2026-11-23`, cursor paging, fields DOI, title, abstract, type, published, subject, author). 388 records, all of type journal-article, 340 with abstracts. Abstract HTML tags were stripped. Each keyword was matched with a Python regular expression, case-insensitive, over title plus abstract, counting a record once; shares divide by 340. The two first-person expressions are the exception: they were run over the abstract text alone, not title plus abstract (recomputed 2026-11-23: 316 and 21 on abstracts alone; 318 and 31 on title plus abstract). Title-only counts run over all 388 titles. OpenAlex counts use group_by queries on `primary_location.source.issn:0018-7267,publication_year:2021-2026` (385 works), no key or email, single requests. The first-person expressions are case-sensitive: any first person `\b(?:I|[Mm]y|[Ww]e|[Oo]ur)\b`, singular `\b(?:I|[Mm]y)\b`. The editorial-board counts come from the HTML table rows of the Wayback copy of the publisher's board page (class "ed-board-member" and its affiliation cell), taking the text after the last comma of each affiliation as the country as printed.

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope**: articles must address work relationships and organizational work processes; papers that do not are "unlikely to be suitable" (Framing Requirements; aims copy 2026-05-02).
- **Review papers**: submitted through the regular route they are desk rejected automatically; they go through the annual special-issue call (Format; guidelines copy 2026-10-03).
- **Length and format**: 13,000 words including abstract and references; manuscripts that exceed it or are formatted incorrectly are sent back (Format).
- **Resubmission and volume limits**: no resubmission after rejection unless the action editor invites it; at most two single-authored manuscripts per 12 months, six months apart (Format).
- **AI**: AI-generated datasets are refused; every AI use must be in the cover letter and methods, and undisclosed use is grounds for rejection or retraction (AI Policy).
- **Anonymisation**: the manuscript must be anonymised with no acknowledgements and third-person self-citation (Peer Review, Format).
- **Shared datasets**: a data transparency matrix and the related manuscripts must be submitted; violation is grounds for rejection (Practical Concerns).

### Soft Tax

- **Selectivity**: the journal states it desk rejects about half of submissions and accepted 3% of 1,587 submissions in 2025 (live statistics page, 2026-11-23; 3% of 1,415 in 2023 in the older copy) (Metrics). Time is therefore spent mostly on first-stage fit.
- **Time**: the only turnaround data are SciRev's n=2 (immediate rejection after 7 days; one full-review rejection after 5.9 weeks); no time-to-acceptance exists (Review Cycle Time).
- **Cover-letter work**: authors must say which journal papers they build on and, for shared data, supply overlap tables (Framing Requirements, Format).
- **Prior online posting**: online publication of an earlier version is barred except institutional repository and conference proceedings, and the policy text read does not say whether a preprint server counts (Preprint Policy).
- **Open access cost**: gold open access carries an APC whose amount was not read (OpenAlex lists USD 3900 / GBP 2859, unverified; Open Access).

### Best Suited For

- Empirical organization research with a clear theoretical contribution about work relationships, using interviews or ethnography (15.9% and 9.4% of abstract records) or multi-wave or multilevel quantitative designs (10.9% and 5.3%) (Methodological Preferences).
- Quantitative work that avoids single-respondent cross-sections, which the journal names as the common reason for rejection (Framing Requirements).
- Conceptual papers that make a substantive theoretical contribution (13.2% of abstract records carry theory-building terms; aims copy) (Methodological Preferences).
- Topics around leadership, employees, emotion, identity, power, gender and labour, which appear in 15.6%, 27.4%, 16.2%, 12.1%, 12.9%, 13.8% and 14.7% of abstract records (Epistemological, Sensitive Topics).
- Meta-analyses and, through the annual call, critical reviews, which the aims page names as accepted types (Format).

### Not Recommended For

- Papers that mainly report scores or relationships between measures, or that are about instruments or research design, which the guidelines say are not suitable (Framing Requirements).
- Student-only simulation studies as the sole basis, which the guidelines say cannot support a paper (Framing Requirements).
- Anyone planning book reviews: the journal does not publish them (Format, policies copy 2025-05-03).
- Authors needing a verified turnaround figure before choosing: none exists beyond SciRev n=2 (Review Cycle Time).
- Authors unwilling to disclose AI use in two places (AI Policy).
